items.title: Tata Sons board members to visit Air India HQ, review performance on Nov 19
items.rss_summary: Tata Sons board members, including Chairman N Chandrasekaran and Noel Tata, will be visiting Air India headquarters in Gurugram on Thursday, according to sources. Air India is co-owned by Tata Sons and Singapore Airlines, which holds a 25.1 per cent stake. The sources said the members will be reviewing the performance of the loss-making Air India. The airline's MD and CEO Tewolde Gebremariam will be making a presentation to the members, they added. Besides, operational integration of Air India and Air India Express is likely to be discussed, the sources said. Tata Sons Chairman Chandrasekaran, board member Noel Tata and others will be visiting the Air India headquarters on Thursday, they added. It could not be immediately ascertained whether all the Tata Sons board members will be visiting the airline's headquarters. items.title: Gold imports may fall to $40 bn in FY27 on duty hike: Commerce Secy
items.rss_summary: India's gold imports in the current fiscal could decline to USD 40 billion, down from about USD 72 billion in FY26, as the duty hike has helped slow inbound shipments, a top official said on Wednesday. Commerce Secretary Rajesh Agrawal said the duty hike effected from May has "slowed down" gold imports "a bit" so far this year, from around USD 60 billion every year. This has also helped manage the trade deficit, he said. In May, the government had hiked import duty on gold and silver to 15 per cent, from 6 per cent, to contain non-essential imports. India imported USD 71.98 billion gold in FY26, up from USD 58.01 billion in FY25. Gold imports declined about 40 per cent to USD 24.78 billion during April-October this year, from about USD 41.24 billion in the corresponding period in 2025. "I think... this year we will end up with USD 35-40 billion of gold imports. I think that is manageable in the current year... The current duty structure has a positive impact on the gold import," .
